newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow phone co MGTS cuts off plane-maker Yakovlev.
newsitem.headline: Moscow phone co MGTS cuts off plane-maker Yakovlev.

text.p: Moscow telephone company MGTS has cut off almost all telephones at Russian plane-maker Yakovlev's headquarters, an MGTS spokeswoman said on Monday.
Anna Boiko told Reuters that about 50 telephones had been cut off because of Yakovlev's outstanding telephone bill.
She did not say how much Yakovlev owed OAO Moskovskaya Gorodskaya Telefonnaya Set (MGTS).
A few phones are still working, she said.
"We do not plan to switch them off although the company has not paid its telephones bill," she said.
A reception secretary at Yakovlev confirmed that most telephones were not working.
The Russian economy is crippled by a web of unpaid bills. Many companies owe each other and the government money, and the government in turn owes many companies money.

The government and some corporations have recently got tough, with companies cutting off services to companies not paying their bills, and the government threatening to have tax-debtors declared bankrupt.

Aviatsionnaya Korporatsiya Yakovlev used to be the Soviet Union's foremost designer of military aircraft and still designs naval fighter planes. It also designs passenger aircraft and produced the short-range Yak-40 and Yak-42 models.
Earlier this year Yakovlev said it was interested in buying bankrupt Dutch aircraft maker Fokker for 370 million guilders ($214.3 million), and Yakovlev officials have visited the Netherlands.

A group of Russian government experts recommended in September that the Russian government back an acquisition. But the cabinet must still take a final decision on the proposal and it is not clear how an acquisition would be funded.
Prospects for relaunching Fokker are poor after a key supplier cut off relations, but it is still in talks with South Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries about a takeover.
